exam_relations.differing_decision: Both convert equal positive sine/cosine coefficients to Rcos(theta-alpha), choose the positive amplitude and acute phase, and return that form. The source coefficients 1,1 are scaled to 3,3 in the exam.
The source and exam use the same expression 2sin(theta)+sqrt(5)cos(theta) and the same Rsin(theta+alpha) template. Compare coefficients, obtain R and the acute phase to the requested precision.

exam_relations.rejection_reason: The source only returns R and phase; the exam states attained maximum/minimum ordinates from the already established R-form. Conversion constants and extreme values are different responses.

exam_relations.differing_decision: Both convert a positive cosine coefficient minus a positive sine coefficient to Rcos(theta+alpha). Coefficient values and requested rounding change; coefficient matching and phase sign decisions remain the same.

r5_examination_relation.reason: The observed R-conversion followed by an original equation anchors the chain. Textbook standalone conversion,reciprocal preprocessing and changed multiple-argument windows remain different structural branches. families.givens_and_unknowns: Linear sine/cosine combination with target and bounded interval.
families.constraints: Retain the original common domain, natural reciprocal zeros/poles, exact angle unit and bounded endpoints. Any introduced division or inverse branch requires a check. families.representation_and_response: R-form followed by finite original-angle roots.
families.scaffolding_and_connected_parts: If the second part changes a coefficient sign, it is a new expression. YMTry20Q1 key solves the plus version although the stem has minus.
families.alternative_methods: Coefficient comparison then shifted sine/cosine roots; direct original-function verification.
families.units_and_precision: Keep exact R and an unrounded internal phase; display the phase and roots at their separately stated precisions. Preserve each original degree/radian unit and endpoint inclusion.
families.answer_form: R, phase and all roots.
families.difficulty_progression: Begin with an exact radian phase and two ordinary branches, then use a rounded degree phase without premature rounding; finally check shifted interval endpoints and all admissible representatives.
families.distinction_basis: Compared with rform-multiple-cycles: Recover roots over the given single-cycle angle interval; the sibling replaces the input by 2x or 3x and must enumerate extra cycles.

families.learner_decisions: First determine the complete inner interval; then optimise the actual reciprocal/square/cube/shift over that interval.

families.constraints: Retain the original common domain, natural reciprocal zeros/poles, exact angle unit and bounded endpoints. Any introduced division or inverse branch requires a check. families.scaffolding_and_connected_parts: A square minimum may occur at inner zero; a reciprocal denominator must not cross zero.
families.alternative_methods: Interval mapping and monotonicity/zero testing, not blindly substituting both endpoints.
families.units_and_precision: Trigonometric ratios and identity coefficients stay exact and dimensionless. families.difficulty_progression: Begin with monotone reciprocal range reversal, then map the interval through a square and check whether zero lies inside; finally combine the square or cube with the stated outer shift.

families.title: Recover formula constants from given extrema and sign conditions
families.learner_decisions: Infer the midline and signed scale from extrema, then state amplitude/intercept and any requested sketch.
families.givens_and_unknowns: Maximum/minimum of a named sine/cosine formula with explicit positive coefficients.
families.constraints: Retain the actual degree/radian unit, strict/closed endpoints and original natural domain. Tangent/reciprocal poles remain excluded after algebra. Exact and decimal answers are distinct instructions. Preserve all registered print/key defects.
families.representation_and_response: Numerical features to constants and optional sketch.
families.scaffolding_and_connected_parts: Keep the sign restriction; a cosine intercept is not generally the midline.
families.alternative_methods: Solve midline plus/minus amplitude equations; substitute in original formula.
families.units_and_precision: Keep graph periods, poles, labelled coordinates and source angular units consistent. Ratio identities remain exact; numerical inverse-angle outputs use the member’s stated precision only after the valid branches have been selected.  Required response: All constants/features and the requested reflected cosine sketch.
families.answer_form: All constants/features and the requested reflected cosine sketch.
families.difficulty_progression: Begin by recovering a midline and positive scale from extrema, then allow a negative cosine coefficient; finally draw the requested graph consistently with the recovered parameters.

families.title: Solve bounded basic or reciprocal trig equations
families.learner_decisions: Find admissible ratio values, recover every representative in the original interval and discard poles.
families.givens_and_unknowns: Single trig/reciprocal equation with explicit degree/radian interval.
families.constraints: Retain the actual degree/radian unit, strict/closed endpoints and original natural domain. Tangent/reciprocal poles remain excluded after algebra. Exact and decimal answers are distinct instructions. Preserve all registered print/key defects.
families.representation_and_response: Equation to complete finite root list.
families.scaffolding_and_connected_parts: The principal calculator value is a starting representative, not the full solution.
families.alternative_methods: Graph or reference-angle/quadrant enumeration independently checked in the original equation.
families.units_and_precision: Keep graph periods, poles, labelled coordinates and source angular units consistent. Ratio identities remain exact; numerical inverse-angle outputs use the member’s stated precision only after the valid branches have been selected.  Required response: All roots in the literal interval with required precision.
families.answer_form: All roots in the literal interval with required precision.
families.difficulty_progression: Begin with a positive degree interval, then use a radian interval; finally enumerate representatives on a negative or asymmetric bounded window and check its endpoints.
families.distinction_basis: Compared with bounded-squared-ratio: Compared with bounded-squared-ratio: Ordinary values vary within a type; changing the window is an explicit bounded-enumeration branch.

families.learner_decisions: Identify powers, distribute signs and combine like terms; recognise cancellations without inventing a division task.
families.givens_and_unknowns: Explicit polynomial operands; unknown simplified polynomial or degree.

families.scaffolding_and_connected_parts: These are prerequisites for theorem/division tasks, not direct coverage of those demands.
families.alternative_methods: Column arithmetic, direct expansion, common factors, difference of squares or telescoping when justified.
families.units_and_precision: Polynomial coefficients, remainders and factors remain exact; roots are returned as exact real values where possible. Required response: An equivalent simplified polynomial, or the explicitly requested degree.
families.answer_form: An equivalent simplified polynomial, or the explicitly requested degree.
families.difficulty_progression: Begin with polynomial addition, then distribute subtraction across every term; finally exploit cancellation of high powers or a telescoping product before combining like terms.
families.distinction_basis: Compared with algebra-binomial-square-support: Distribute polynomial arithmetic and exploit like-term cancellation; the binomial-square sibling has to retain the mixed term in a squared two-term expression.

exam_relations.differing_decision: Selected Goldie1C Q1(iii), |3-x|=4, and the target |3x-1|=4 both open the plus/minus branches of one affine absolute value, solve the two linear equations and retain both admissible scalar roots. Only coefficients change.

The source solves one affine absolute value directly. The target must reuse its preceding roots as exponential values, reject any nonpositive intermediate and take logs to recover the exponent. These are additional target preimage decisions.

The source has a fixed positive right side and two direct linear branches. The target find symbolic intersection coordinates of a modulus graph and a signed straight line, so its variable signed right side needs a nonnegativity/branch check and back-substitution for the ordinate. The source omits those decisions.

The source has a fixed positive right side and two direct linear branches. The target equate exponential bases to obtain |1-x|=3x and solve the modulus-linear equation with valid signs, so its variable signed right side needs a nonnegativity/branch check after the exponential-base reduction. The source omits those decisions.

families.title: Normalise a nonzero vector and apply a specified magnitude
families.learner_decisions: Compute the positive norm,choose allowed direction sign and scale to the requested length.
families.givens_and_unknowns: Nonzero vector,direction or a derived position; unknown unit vector or prescribed-length parallel vector.
families.constraints: Zero vector cannot be normalised. SAME direction selects positive multiplier;parallel-only admits either sign unless the source adds a condition.
families.representation_and_response: Vectors/positions to exact normalised or scaled vector.
families.scaffolding_and_connected_parts: A joining/midpoint/extended-ray position may need recovery first;that geometry remains attached.
families.alternative_methods: Divide by Euclidean norm then multiply requested magnitude;check norm and parallelism independently.
families.units_and_precision: Vector components and displacement coordinates retain the source length scale, while a unit vector is dimensionless. Norms and dot products stay exact until a requested angle or length rounding; directed inclination, bearing and acute line angle retain distinct conventions. The resulting unit vector is dimensionless; a prescribed-length vector retains that length unit. Required response: Exact vector of required norm/direction,plus any other named outputs.
families.answer_form: Exact vector of required norm/direction,plus any other named outputs.
families.difficulty_progression: Begin by normalising a nonzero vector, then scale it to a prescribed length and same direction; finally distinguish a parallel-only request admitting both signs and derive an externally located vector before normalising it.
families.distinction_basis: Compared with vector-magnitude: Compared with vector-magnitude: Normalisation and sign convention are additional decisions beyond raw magnitude.

families.title: Find the angle between supplied nonzero directions
families.learner_decisions: Compute signed dot and both positive norms,then select the angle convention actually requested.
families.givens_and_unknowns: Two supplied vectors,or directions explicitly given inside an additional formal line representation; unknown angle/cosine.
families.constraints: Nonzero directions;clamp only numericalround-off,not invalid data. Between-vector angle can be obtuse/180degrees;acute line angle is separately specified.
families.representation_and_response: Vectors/given direction columns to exact cosine or rounded angle.
families.scaffolding_and_connected_parts: Formal vector-line/skew-line manipulation is additional scope;only explicitly supplied direction calculations are retained from those sources.
families.alternative_methods: Scalar-product cosine or exact geometric check;prescribed scalar-product instructions remain.
families.units_and_precision: Vector components and displacement coordinates retain the source length scale, while a unit vector is dimensionless. Norms and dot products stay exact until a requested angle or length rounding; directed inclination, bearing and acute line angle retain distinct conventions. The between-vector angle uses the signed dot product and two positive norms. Required response: Requested angle/cosine with correct directed/acute convention.
families.answer_form: Requested angle/cosine with correct directed/acute convention.
families.difficulty_progression: Begin with two supplied directions and their dot product, then retain an obtuse or opposite-vector angle; finally apply the explicitly requested acute line convention in the retained supplied-direction facet.
families.distinction_basis: Compared with vector-angle-at-point: Compared with vector-angle-at-point: Angle convention and source direction availability are meaningful branches,not permission to author formal vector-line questions.
